title: The Quintupling Gravel Wight
story: Deep in the Slatefall Quarry, Mr 6 meets Obscarrow, a wight made of rattling gravel. Every time a blade strikes him, each pebble-self bursts into five — and there are already 4 of him grinning in the dust. The quarry gate's warding circle can only seal away a crowd of 500 or fewer.
question: Starting from 4 wights, how many wights will there be after Mr 6 strikes exactly three times?
solution: After three strikes: 100 x 5 = 500 wights — exactly the circle's limit.
praise: Multiplying by 5 was spot on — the crowd just needed one more round of growing before you stopped counting.
hint: Each strike multiplies the whole crowd by 5. Do it one strike at a time and write down each number.
victory: Mr 6 struck three times, then simply stepped aside — 500 gravel wights tumbled into the warding circle, which snapped shut with a satisfied click. 'Outnumbered,' said Mr 6, 'is not the same as outsmarted.'
imagePrompt: A vast moonlit slate quarry swarming with hundreds of grinning gravel-pebble wights funneling toward a glowing rune circle, as a small numeral-6 knight calmly sheathes his sword on a ledge above.
